q: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023?
ex:
{{

Four Delimitation Commissions have been constituted: Delimitation Commissions have been set up 4 times in India till December 2023—in 1952 (under the Delimitation Commission Act, 1952), in 1963 (under the Delimitation Commission Act, 1962), in 1973 (under the Delimitation Act, 1972), and in 2002 (under the Delimitation Act, 2002).

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q:
The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992 amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
1. Konkani
2. Manipuri
3. Nepali
4. Maithili

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: The 71st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

Maithili (along with Bodo, Dogri, and Santhali) was subsequently added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:
Which of the following statements are correct about the Constitution of India?
1. Powers of the Municipalities are given in Part IX A of the Constitution.
2. Emergency provisions are given in Part XVIII of the Constitution.
3. Provisions related to the amendment of the Constitution are given in Part XX of the Constitution.

Select the answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

All three statements are correct:

  • Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) contains provisions governing the Municipalities.
  • Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) details Emergency provisions.
  • Part XX (Article 368) outlines the procedure for the Amendment of the Constitution.

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q: Which one of the following statements is correct as per the Constitution of India?
options: Inter-State trade and commerce is a State subject under the State List.
Inter-State migration is a State subject under the State List.
Inter-State quarantine is a Union subject under the Union List.
Corporation tax is a State subject under the State List.
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 3: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, Inter-State quarantine is explicitly placed under Entry 81 of List I (Union List).

Inter-State trade and commerce (Entry 42), Inter-State migration (Entry 81), and Corporation tax (Entry 85) are also subjects under the Union List, not the State List.

}}

q: Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy?
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 4: In the landmark nine-judge Constitution Bench judgment in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court unanimously affirmed that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution.

}}

q:
What are the duties of the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) as Head of the Department of Military Affairs?
1. Permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee
2. Exercise military command over the three Service Chiefs
3. Principal Military Advisor to Defence Minister on all tri-service matters

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 1 and 3 are correct: The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) serves as the permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and acts as the Principal Military Advisor to the Raksha Mantri on all tri-service operational matters.

Statement 2 is incorrect: The CDS does not exercise direct operational military command over the three individual Service Chiefs, who maintain independent administrative command of their respective forces.

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q: Operations undertaken by the Army towards upliftment of the local population in remote areas to include addressing of their basic needs is called:
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 3: Operation Sadbhavana (Goodwill) is an initiative launched by the Indian Army in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh to improve infrastructure, education, and health for local populations in remote border areas.

Operation Sankalp is a naval maritime security mission in the Persian Gulf; Operation Maitri was the Nepal earthquake rescue operation; and Operation Madad refers to disaster relief during floods.

}}

q: The longest border between any two countries in the world is between:
options: Canada and the United States of America
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 1: The international border between Canada and the United States of America is the longest land border between any two nations in the world, spanning approximately 8,890 kilometers (including the boundary along Alaska).

}}

q:
Which of the following statements about the Ethics Committee in the Lok Sabha are correct?
1. Initially it was an ad-hoc Committee.
2. Only a Member of the Lok Sabha can make a complaint relating to unethical conduct of a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. This Committee cannot take up any matter which is sub-judice.

Select the answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 1 and 3 are correct: The Ethics Committee was initially constituted as an ad-hoc body in the year 2000 before becoming a permanent committee. The Committee does not take up matters that are sub-judice before a court of law.

Statement 2 is incorrect: Any person from the general public can submit a complaint against a Member, provided it is submitted through a Member of Lok Sabha or accompanied by an affidavit.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: Who was the Provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Dr. Rajendra Prasad took over?
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 4: When the Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on December 9, 1946, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member present, was chosen as the temporary (provisional) President following French democratic practice, before Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as permanent President on December 11, 1946.

}}

q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for the establishment of an All India Federation based on the union of the British Indian Provinces and Princely States.
2. Defence and Foreign Affairs were kept under the control of the federal legislature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 1 is correct: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the establishment of an All India Federation comprising British Indian provinces and princely states.

Statement 2 is incorrect: Dyarchy was established at the Centre, under which subjects like Defence and External Affairs were 'Reserved Subjects' exclusively administered by the Governor-General at his discretion, not by the federal legislature.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: Which one of the following is a work attributed to playwright Bhasa?
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 3: Madhyama-vyayoga is a classical Sanskrit play written by the ancient playwright Bhasa, drawing its plot from the Mahabharata.

Kavyalankara was authored by Bhamaha; Natyashastra by Bharata Muni; and Mahabhashya by Patanjali.

}}

q: Sanghabhuti, an Indian Buddhist monk, who travelled to China at the end of the fourth century AD, was the author of a commentary on:
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 3: Sanghabhuti was a Buddhist scholar-monk from Kashmir who travelled to northern China in the late 4th century AD and translated and composed commentaries on the Sarvastivada Vinaya text tradition into Chinese.

}}

q:
Consider the following properties included in the World Heritage List released by UNESCO:
1. Shantiniketan
2. Rani-ki-Vav
3. Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
4. Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodhgaya

How many of the above properties were included in 2023?
ex:
{{

Only two properties were inscribed in 2023:

  • Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura in Karnataka) was inscribed in September 2023 (42nd site).
  • Rani-ki-Vav was inscribed in 2014, and the Mahabodhi Temple Complex was inscribed in 2002.

}}

q:
As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of:
1. Addition
2. Variation
3. Repeal

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

All three elements are correct: Article 368(1) explicitly states: 'Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.'

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Italy
2. Japan
3. Nigeria
4. South Korea
5. South Africa

Which of the above countries are frequently mentioned in the media for their low birth rates, or ageing population or declining population?
ex:

Countries 1, 2, and 4: Italy, Japan, and South Korea face severe demographic decline and low total fertility rates (with South Korea recording the lowest fertility rate globally at ~0.72).

Nigeria and South Africa have young populations with high fertility rates.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:
Which of the following statements are correct in respect of a Money Bill in the Parliament?
1. Article 109 mentions special procedure in respect of Money Bills.
2. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.
3. The Rajya Sabha can either approve the Bill or suggest changes but cannot reject it.
4. Amendments to a Money Bill suggested by the Rajya Sabha have to be accepted by the Lok Sabha.

Select the answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Article 109 prescribes the special legislative procedure for Money Bills. Money Bills can only originate in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend the Bill; it can only return it with recommendations within 14 days.

Statement 4 is incorrect: The Lok Sabha is not obligated to accept recommendations from the Rajya Sabha and may reject all or any of them.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

}}

q:
The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members?
1. Governor of the Constituent State
2. Chief Minister of the Constituent State
3. Three Members to be nominated by the President of India
4. The Home Minister of India

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Under Section 3 of the amended North Eastern Council Act, the statutory composition of the Council includes the Governors and Chief Ministers of the eight northeastern states and three members nominated by the President of India.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam':
1. Provisions will come into effect from the 18th Lok Sabha.
2. This will be in force for 15 years after becoming an Act.
3. There are provisions for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes Women within the quota reserved for the Scheduled Castes.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
ex:
{{

Statements 2 and 3 are correct: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for an initial duration of 15 years, and includes horizontal sub-reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes women within their respective quotas.

Statement 1 is incorrect: The Act specifies that the reservation will take effect only after a delimitation exercise is conducted based on relevant figures from the first Census held after the commencement of the Act, not immediately for the 18th Lok Sabha.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:
Which of the following statements about 'Exercise Mitra Shakti-2023' are correct?
1. This was a joint military exercise between India and Bangladesh.
2. It commenced in Aundh (Pune).
3. Joint response during counter-terrorism operations was a goal of this operation.
4. Indian Air Force was a part of this exercise.

Select the answer using the code given below:
ex:
{{

Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: The 9th edition of Exercise Mitra Shakti-2023 took place in Aundh (Pune), focused on counter-terrorism operations in semi-urban environments, and integrated air force personnel from both sides.

Statement 1 is incorrect: Exercise Mitra Shakti is conducted between India and Sri Lanka (the India-Bangladesh exercise is named Sampriti).

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q: A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to:
options: a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action.
the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition.
the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case.
the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy.
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 3: The Writ of Prohibition ('to forbid') is issued by a higher judicial court (Supreme Court under Article 32 or High Court under Article 226) to an inferior court or quasi-judicial tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping jurisdiction that it does not legally possess.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. It is the Governor of the State who recognizes and declares any community of that State as a Scheduled Tribe.
2. A community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in a State need not be so in another State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 2 is correct: Scheduled Tribe status is State/UT-specific; a tribal community recognized as an ST in one State is not automatically recognized as an ST in another State.

Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Article 342(1), the President of India (after consultation with the Governor of the State) specifies and notifies the list of Scheduled Tribes.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
With reference to Union Budget, consider the following statements:
1. The Union Finance Minister on behalf of the Prime Minister lays the Annual Financial Statement before both the Houses of Parliament.
2. At the Union level, no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 113(3) of the Constitution of India, no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President of India.

Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Article 112, the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before Parliament by the Union Finance Minister on behalf of the President of India, not the Prime Minister.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: If the United States of America (USA) were to default on its debt, holders of US Treasury Bonds will not be able to exercise their claims to receive payment.
Statement II: The USA Government debt is not backed by any hard assets, but only by the faith of the Government.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
ex:
{{

Statement I is incorrect: Bondholders would still possess valid legal claims to demand and receive payment even in the event of default.

Statement II is correct: US Treasury debt is not collateralized by physical assets/gold, but is backed by the full faith and credit of the US Government.

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Syndicated lending spreads the risk of borrower default across multiple lenders.
Statement II: The syndicated loan can be fixed amount/lump sum of funds, but cannot be a credit line.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
ex:

Statement I is correct: A loan syndicate distributes the exposure and credit risk among multiple financial institutions.

Statement II is incorrect: Syndicated financing can be structured as fixed term loans, revolving credit lines, or combinations of both.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the digital rupee:
1. It is a sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment with its monetary policy.
2. It appears as a liability on the RBI's balance sheet.
3. It is insured against inflation by its very design.
4. It is freely convertible against commercial bank money and cash.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
ex:
{{

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC/Digital Rupee) is sovereign legal tender issued by the RBI, recorded as a central bank liability, and freely exchangeable 1:1 with fiat physical cash and bank deposits.

Statement 3 is incorrect: The digital rupee holds no automatic built-in hedge or insurance against macroeconomic price inflation.

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q:

3. Tathagata

Statement 1 is incorrect: Nayaputta (Nathaputta) was the epithet used for Vardhamana Mahavira (referring to his Jnatrika/Naya clan).

q: Who of the following rulers of medieval India gave permission to the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal?

q:
With reference to revenue collection by Cornwallis, consider the following statements:
1. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities.
2. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state, on or before the fixed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 2 is correct: Under the Permanent Settlement's 'Sunset Law', failure to deposit the fixed revenue by sunset on the appointed date resulted in forfeiture and public auction of the Zamindari estate.

Statement 1 is incorrect: The Ryotwari system rigidly demanded revenue regardless of floods, droughts, or crop failures.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. There are no parables in Upanishads.
2. Upanishads were composed earlier than the Puranas.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 2 is correct: The Vedic Upanishads were composed roughly between the 8th and 4th centuries BCE, whereas the classical Puranas reached their canonical forms much later between the 3rd and 10th centuries CE.

Statement 1 is incorrect: The Upanishads contain famous allegorical parables, such as the 'Parable of the Two Birds on the Same Tree' (Mundaka/Svetasvatara Upanishad).

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct

q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: India does not import apples from the United States of America.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
ex:

Statement I is incorrect: India imports significant volumes of apples from the US, especially following the reduction of retaliatory tariffs in September 2023.

q:
While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration, consider the following statements:
1. He/She shall not preside.
2. He/She shall not have the right to speak.
3. He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 96(1), the Speaker cannot preside when a resolution for their removal is being considered.

Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect: Under Article 96(2), the Speaker retains the right to speak, take part in the proceedings, and cast a vote in the first instance (though not a casting vote in case of equality of votes).

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:
With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution.
2. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
3. A bill in regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ex:
{{

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Bills originating/pending in the Lok Sabha or passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapse upon dissolution under Article 107.

Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 108(5), if the President has already notified the intention to summon a joint sitting prior to dissolution, the bill does not lapse and can proceed to the joint sitting.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:
1. Prorogation of a House by the President of India does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers.
2. Prorogation of a House is generally done after the House is adjourned sine die but there is no bar to the President of India proroguing the House which is in session.
3. Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is done by the President of India who, save in exceptional circumstances, does so on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
ex:
{{

Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Prorogation typically follows sine die adjournment, but the President retains power to prorogue an active session. Dissolution is performed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet.

Statement 1 is incorrect: The President exercises the power to summon and prorogue Parliament strictly on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:

q:

q: With reference to ancient Indian society, what was the primary distinguishing feature of the 'Anuloma' form of marriage described in the Dharmashastras?
options: Marriage between a man of a higher Varna and a woman of a lower Varna
Marriage between a woman of a higher Varna and a man of a lower Varna
Marriage conducted by abduction of the bride following armed battle
Marriage where the bride's father receives a voluntary pair of kine from the groom
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 1: In ancient Dharmashastra legal texts, an Anuloma union (with the grain) occurs when a man marries a woman from a Varna lower than his own, which was generally tolerated.

A Pratiloma union (against the grain) occurred when a woman married a man from a lower Varna, which was strongly disapproved of in orthodox texts.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Special Drawing Rights' (SDR) of the International Monetary Fund:
1. The SDR is an international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves.
2. The value of the SDR is based on a basket of five currencies: US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, and British Pound Sterling.
3. The SDR is a direct currency and holds a legal claim against the physical assets of the IMF.
ex:
{{

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The SDR is an international accounting reserve asset whose valuation basket comprises five major currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP).

Statement 3 is incorrect: The SDR is neither a physical currency nor a claim on the IMF; rather, it represents a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of IMF member states.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: With reference to the medieval architecture of the Delhi Sultanate, the 'Tughlaq Style' of building was structurally characterized by which of the following engineering techniques?
options: Extensive use of pure white Makrana marble and double-domes
Sloping batter walls (slanted thick masonry walls) and rugged grey quartzite stone construction
Delicate pierced marble latticework (Jali) with pietra dura floral inlays
Freestanding multistoried wooden pavilions without stone foundations
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 2: Architecture of the Tughlaq period (e.g., Tughlaqabad Fort and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's Tomb) is characterized by massive, austere stone engineering featuring signature sloping/battered outer walls (to provide structural strength and illusion of height), using grey quartzite and red sandstone, avoiding lavish decorative carving.

}}
